sections.html:
Denver is Colorado's capital and largest city, in the South Platte River valley just east of the Front Range. The 2020 census counted 715,522 residents, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 740,613. The city is also a county. It has been a consolidated city and county since 1902, so one government assesses, taxes and records property. That leaves fewer offices for a seller to chase than in most Colorado towns.

Fewer than half of Denver homes, 48.8%, are owner-occupied, across 335,428 households (2020 to 2024). The median owner-occupied value is $616,000 and median gross rent is $1,831. With that mix, many sellers are landlords, heirs or people who bought a rental and now want out. The median is a citywide marker. Your own price will swing with condition, neighborhood and lot size.

Hail is the weather risk that hits Denver roofs hardest. Among U.S. cities with at least 50,000 people, Denver ranks 10th for hail proneness and has seen three of the ten costliest hailstorms in the country. Snow averages 53.5 inches a year, July highs run about 89.9 degrees, and the record high is 105 degrees, set June 28, 2018.

A damaged roof, cracked siding or an unrepaired insurance claim can slow a traditional sale, because buyers' lenders and inspectors look hard at roofs. Sellers get asked:

  • Was the hail damage ever claimed and repaired, or just left?
  • How old is the roof, and will a buyer's insurer cover it?
  • Do sun and freeze-thaw cycles show up in the stucco, deck or exterior paint?

Answer with paperwork if you have it. A cash buyer will take the house with the damage included.

Denver bills taxes in arrears, after the year they cover, and the city's Treasury Division collects them.

Payment optionDue date
First installmentLast day of February
Second installmentJune 15
Single full paymentApril 30

A date that falls on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day. Statements are online: search your address in Denver's property search tool, open the Tax Documents section and download the year's statement. A credit or debit card adds a 2.5% service fee, while an electronic check avoids it. Treasury's phone number is 720-913-9300.

The title company usually prorates the current year's taxes between you and the buyer. Treasury also issues a Certificate of Taxes Due for Real Property, which title companies use to see what is owed on a parcel. Unpaid prior years must be cleared before a clean transfer. For appeal rights and assessment timing, visit the Denver Treasury property tax page.

sections.h2: The state fee on a Denver deed
sections.html: Colorado charges a documentary fee of $0.01 per $100 on transfer deeds when the consideration is more than $500. County recording pages describe it that way. Denver records deeds in the same county system, so the fee, the recording charge and any transfer paperwork all appear on the settlement statement. Going with a cash buyer does not change those steps, though it can shorten the gap between signing and recording, since no lender has to fund a loan first.

Denver requires a license for every short-term rental, and the rental has to be the host's primary residence. Hosts must show their business license number in every advertisement, and anyone who breaks the rules can be fined or lose the license.

That matters if you own a second Denver property that ran as an Airbnb. Under a primary-residence rule, a house the owner does not live in cannot lawfully operate as a short-term rental, so it may have to be sold or turned into a long-term rental. A buyer who counted on nightly income may value it less. Check the city's rental, zoning and licensing pages for your address before you list or accept an offer.

Steady public-sector, hospital and airline jobs keep housing demand strong near downtown, but they do not shield any one owner from a layoff, a divorce or an inherited house nobody wants to manage. Those events, more than the market, are what push most Denver owners to sell quickly.

If you inherited a house, gather the paperwork that proves who can sign, then ask the title company what it needs before it will schedule a closing. If you are a landlord with a tenant in place, find out early whether the buyer will take the house occupied. A cash buyer often will.

sections.h2: Steps in a Denver cash sale
sections.html:
1. You describe the house and send the address.
  2. We review it and give you a written offer.
  3. You accept, and a title company searches the record, asks Treasury for the Certificate of Taxes Due and prepares the deed.
  4. You sign, the deed is recorded, and you are paid.

You can compare the offer with a listing before you decide, and declining costs nothing. Have your tax statement handy. You can download it from the property search tool in a few minutes.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Denver house?
sections.html:
Most owners choose between listing with an agent, selling on their own and accepting a cash purchase. Each trades price against time and effort.

  • Listing with an agent: usually the highest price on a house in good condition, with showings, post-inspection repair requests and a buyer's loan approval to wait for.
  • Selling on your own: saves the agent's commission but leaves pricing, disclosures and paperwork to you.
  • Cash sale: a buyer purchases the house as it stands, so there is no repair list and you can often pick the closing date.

A cash route suits a house with deferred maintenance, a hail-damaged roof, a tenant in place or an estate that needs to settle. A listing suits a clean house with time on the calendar. Compare both before deciding. A cash offer from us carries no obligation.

faqs.q: How much is the median home worth in Denver?
faqs.a: The 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied homes is $616,000. Individual houses vary widely with condition, neighborhood and lot size, so treat it as a citywide benchmark.

faqs.q: When are Denver property taxes due?
faqs.a: The last day of February and June 15 for two installments, or April 30 for one full payment. A due date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Denver house that was used as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Yes. Denver requires a license and a primary-residence host, so a house that lacked either may have compliance issues a buyer will ask about. A cash buyer can purchase it as it stands, though you should settle any city fines or unpaid taxes.

faqs.q: Does hail damage stop me from selling a house in Denver?
faqs.a: No. Denver is among the most hail-prone large cities, so buyers expect to see it. A damaged roof can lower the price or complicate a buyer's financing, which is why many owners with roof damage consider an as-is cash sale.

faqs.q: What is the state documentary fee in Colorado?
faqs.a: It is $0.01 per $100 of consideration on a deed over $500, as county recording pages describe it. It appears on the settlement statement.
